Tsimdo (Tigrinya ጽምዶ, 'engagement'/'alignment') is a genuine named entity documented by The Africa Report, IDN-InDepthNews and Ethiopian state media, but an ALLEGED and informal one: neither Asmara nor the TPLF has confirmed a formal alliance, its accused members call it a political fiction, and the realignment involves the TPLF's hardliner (Debretsion) wing rather than the whole front. Its alleged membership is also broader than TPLF and Eritrea, extending to Sudan, Fano and the OLA. Saudi Arabia and Egypt have backed Eritrea and by extension the TPLF hardliners to counter Abiy Ahmed's Red Sea port ambitions. No source names a specific town; the coordinate is Adigrat, an analyst inference as the principal city on the Zalambesa-Adigrat corridor.

title: ISWAP ambush kills four soldiers between Yamtake and Bitta, Borno
summary: Suspected ISWAP fighters ambushed a Nigerian military element on the road between Yamtake and Bitta in Gwoza LGA, Borno State, using small arms and improvised explosive devices. At least four soldiers were killed and several wounded, with three military vehicles destroyed and weapons and ammunition seized. PROVISIONAL: all reporting traces to a single origin (an analyst's social-media post amplifying ISWAP claim imagery); no Nigerian military confirmation and no independent wire corroboration.

title: RSF killings and night raids escalate in El Nuhud amid reinforcement buildup
summary: Residents reported at least four civilians shot dead over three days and a wave of night raids and arrests in El Nuhud as RSF reinforcements poured into the town over the preceding fortnight. Sudan Tribune and Youm7 independently reported large RSF reinforcement columns from Darfur, an arrest campaign against alleged army affiliates, and nine RSF positions inside residential neighbourhoods. El Nuhud is the key logistical hub linking Kordofan to Darfur, and the buildup followed the army's 25-26 July recapture of Bara, Jabrat al-Sheikh, Um Qirfa and Um Sayala in North Kordofan.

title: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegation convoy on Torit-Magwi road
summary: Unknown gunmen ambushed a convoy carrying an SPLM delegation near Tutumore on the Torit-Magwi road, killing driver Adolfo Ngachan and wounding delegation member Emilio Iga and a bodyguard. SPLM deputy chairperson Dr. Margaret Itto Leonardo escaped unharmed. The delegation was travelling to Pageri, Magwi County, for party membership registration ahead of the 22 December 2026 elections. No group claimed responsibility; state officials described the attackers as unknown criminals on a road with a documented pattern of banditry.

title: Houthi ballistic missile salvo devastates government camps in Hadramawt and Marib
summary: Houthi forces fired eight ballistic missiles from al-Jawf governorate into the al-Thiniya and al-Abr camps in Hadramawt and the al-Rouk camp in Marib, striking Homeland Shield Forces, Emergency Forces and First Military Region formations. At least 30 government soldiers were killed and 15 wounded in the initial count; medical sources later reported 38 dead and a military source put the toll at 58, while the International Crisis Group cited military sources describing about 50 killed including four Saudi officers. It was described as the fiercest military escalation in Yemen since the 2022 truce. Coordinates anchor on al-Abr in Hadramawt; the event spans three camps across two governorates.

title: Houthi projectiles wound 11 civilians in Saudi border city of Najran
summary: A Houthi projectile attack on the southern Saudi border city of Najran wounded 11 civilians, among them a four-year-old child with second-degree burns as well as Egyptian, Pakistani and Yemeni nationals. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki called the strikes terrorist attacks using indiscriminate projectiles. The projectiles struck late on Thursday 6 August; the coalition announced the casualty toll on 7 August.

title: First round of post-Maduro transition talks opens in Caracas
summary: A first round of US-backed talks opened on 6 August between National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez and opposition figure Dinorah Figuera, aimed at strengthening response to the June earthquakes and expanding political freedoms after the January capture of Nicolás Maduro. Exiled leaders María Corina Machado and Edmundo González did not participate; the round closed on 12 August with agreements on judicial reform and seeking access to frozen funds for earthquake recovery.

title: China confirms two coast guard deaths from 2025 Scarborough Shoal collision
summary: Nearly a year after the China Coast Guard cutter Nanyu collided with the PLA Navy destroyer Guilin while chasing the Philippine vessel BRP Suluan near Scarborough Shoal in August 2025, Beijing publicly confirmed for the first time that two coast guard crewmen, aged 21 and 25, died in the crash. The admission underscored the risks of aggressive intercepts in the disputed shoal, scene of repeated water-cannon incidents against Philippine vessels in July 2026.

title: Anti-Taliban rocket attack on military section of Kabul airport
summary: The Afghanistan Freedom Front claimed a rocket attack at around 20:30 on 6 August on the military section of Kabul international airport, saying it caused heavy damage and casualties; the claim was released and reported on 7 August. The Afghanistan National Independence Front separately claimed the same strike with markedly different figures (four rockets, 10+ Taliban killed), and neither group clarified whether these were one attack or two. The same day the AFF also claimed an attack on a Taliban intelligence headquarters in Police District 6 of Jalalabad, Nangarhar, killing two and wounding one, while the Afghanistan United Front claimed operations in Ghor and Badakhshan. The groups say they have claimed more than 15 attacks in the preceding week; none of the claims have been independently verified and the Taliban did not comment.

title: Afghanistan United Front claims 48-hour attack wave across five provinces
region: Kandahar (multi-province: Kandahar, Helmand, Ghor, Baghlan, Badakhshan)
summary: The Afghanistan United Front said its fighters carried out six operations in Kandahar, Helmand, Ghor, Baghlan and Badakhshan provinces over a 48-hour period, claiming 19 Taliban members killed or wounded including a senior Taliban police officer in Kandahar and a Taliban commander in Helmand. Claimed sites included Band-e Timor in Maywand district and Kandahar city's 15th Security District, Gerdab in Ghor's Al-Farooq district, Pul-e Hesar in Baghlan and Argo in Badakhshan. The group also claimed to have captured two Taliban outposts and seized weapons and ammunition. The Taliban did not comment and no outlet independently verified the claims. For context, a UN Secretary-General assessment covering 1 February to 30 April 2026 found that 16 of 18 attacks claimed by such groups had been verified by the UN.

title: ADF night raid on Banana École village kills 13 in Mambasa
summary: Presumed ADF fighters raided Banana École village at PK20, about 20 km from Mambasa-centre on the Kisangani road, during the night of 7-8 August, killing at least 13 people. The attackers burned shops, two trucks and three motorcycles and abducted 14 residents, leaving the toll provisional.

title: M23 and Wazalendo clash across Ziralo villages near Numbi
summary: FARDC and allied Wazalendo fighters opened an offensive against M23 in Kalehe territory, clashing at Bunje, Chabikere, Mpanama and Katale in the Ziralo grouping. M23 separately blamed pro-government forces for an explosion at Lumbishi, a village between the Ziralo grouping and the Numbi mineral trading hub, opening a week of fighting on the axis. No fatalities were reported for the 7 August clashes; FARDC accused M23 of 82mm mortar fire on Bunje.
source_name: Critical Threats (AEI), Congo War Security Review, August 14, 2026

title: US airstrike targets al-Shabaab near Jilib, southern Somalia
summary: US Africa Command conducted an airstrike against al-Shabaab in the vicinity of Jilib, approximately 322km southwest of Mogadishu, in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia. AFRICOM withheld details of units and assets, citing operational security, and released no battle-damage or casualty assessment. The strike came amid a record-setting tempo of US air operations in Somalia, which reached at least 78 strikes for the year as of 7 August 2026. Distinct from the 30 July strike near Jamaame, 58km northeast of Kismayo.

title: Somali intelligence arrests nine al-Shabaab operatives plotting Mogadishu attacks
summary: Somalia's National Intelligence and Security Agency announced the arrest of nine al-Shabaab members it said were plotting attacks in Mogadishu, one day after the federal government warned of imminent strikes on hotels and government facilities. The suspects were detained in the Garasbaaley and Kaxda districts and parts of Ceelasha Biyaha on the capital's northwestern outskirts, four of them a connected network, and were held pending referral to judicial authorities. The Somali National Army subsequently deployed reinforcements along key roads into the capital. Al-Shabaab carried out more attacks in Mogadishu between 1 and 7 August than in any full month since January 2026, according to ACLED data.

title: Boko Haram night raid kills eight in Kangaleri, Far North Cameroon
summary: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen entered Kangaleri village, a locality of Mora commune in the Mayo-Sava division, at around 11 p.m. on Friday 7 August, killing six residents outright and wounding three, two of whom later died in hospital. The same night, gunmen looted shops and livestock in Tourou in the Mokolo district (Mayo-Tsanaga division) without causing deaths.

title: CRP militia overruns FARDC position at Djukpa, Djugu
summary: Fighters of the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) assaulted an isolated FARDC post at Djukpa, about three kilometres from the Mabanga trading centre in Djugu territory, during the night of 7-8 August, killing two soldiers and seriously wounding three others. Security sources said the raid was aimed at seizing weapons and ammunition.

title: Ethiopian AUSSOM contingent hands Buurhakaba base to Somali army and withdraws
summary: Ethiopian troops serving with AUSSOM Sector 3 formally handed their forward operating base at Buurhakaba, about 185km northwest of Mogadishu by road, to the Somali National Army's 60th Division after nearly twelve years in place since 2014, then withdrew overnight. The town is ringed on every side by al-Shabaab and regional officials publicly doubted the SNA's capacity to hold it alone. The handover was part of an accelerated AU drawdown driven by the mission's funding shortfall, with the AUSSOM mandate expiring 31 December 2026.

title: Iran attacks ADNOC tanker in the Strait of Hormuz
summary: The United Arab Emirates said Iran attacked a tanker belonging to the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company as it transited the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours, causing no casualties. It was one of a series of strikes on ADNOC-linked shipping through August: two more ADNOC-affiliated vessels, the Navig8 Messi and the Tarif, were hit by UAVs on 13 August, and a further vessel on 14 August. The same day, Iran's Supreme National Security Council issued sweeping conditions for reopening the strait, including a permanent end to the war, a US troop withdrawal, lifting of the naval blockade, sanctions relief and full compensation for war damage. No source published the attack position; coordinates are a mid-strait approximation.

title: Yemeni government dawn offensive on Houthi positions in southern Hodeidah
summary: Government forces launched a dawn assault on Houthi command centres and fortifications in contested southern Hodeidah, opening a ground counteroffensive after days of Houthi missile bombardment. Army spokesman Colonel Majed al-Nuzaili said operations along several axes of contact targeted Houthi capabilities and forces to safeguard civilians. No casualty figures were reported for this operation by any source, and ACLED records no standalone entry for it.

title: Kokorat San Ras massacre in Gros-Morne, Artibonite
summary: Members of the Kokorat San Ras gang attacked a remote community in the commune of Gros-Morne over the weekend of 7-8 August, killing at least a dozen residents, according to the commune's mayor. The massacre was part of a surge of renewed gang attacks across Haiti in early August that killed and injured dozens of civilians and stoked concerns over security for upcoming elections.

title: JNIM overruns army barracks in San, Ségou region
summary: JNIM fighters assaulted the Malian army camp in the town of San at around 5:30 a.m., temporarily occupying the barracks and killing roughly 10-12 soldiers before withdrawing. The army said the attack was repelled and the base remained under government control, while JNIM-affiliated channels released video claiming full control; the Malian army's 23rd regiment separately claimed more than 40 attackers were killed. Note: San cercle was legally detached into the new San Region under Law 2023-006, but all reporting including JNIM's own claim uses 'région de Ségou'.

title: Houthi missile and drone barrage on al-Makha port kills seven
summary: Houthi forces struck the Red Sea port city of al-Makha with ballistic missiles and drones on Sunday evening, killing at least seven people - four military and three civilians - and wounding about 30. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the operation targeted Saudi troop concentrations and weapons depots along Yemen's western coast. An earlier wave the same day drove the combined 9 August toll higher and caused the damage to port infrastructure that contributed to al-Makha's later suspension of operations.

title: Fire at Aramco Jizan refinery after claimed Houthi drone strike
summary: A blaze broke out early Sunday at Saudi Aramco's 400,000 bpd Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast after what the Houthis claimed was a precise drone strike. Saudi authorities reported only that the fire was extinguished with no casualties and did not attribute the blaze to an attack; the attack claim rests on Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree, who framed it as retaliation for Saudi drone operations over Yemen's Saada and Hajjah provinces. The refinery had already been shut since a late-July strike and restart slipped to around 30 August. Coordinates anchor on the refinery inside Jazan City for Primary and Downstream Industries, about 45 km north-northwest of Jizan city.

title: Gunmen kill four in Santa Rosa neighborhood of Esmeraldas
summary: Armed men opened fire on people at a residence in the Nuevos Horizontes sector of the Santa Rosa neighborhood in western Esmeraldas city on the night of 9 August, killing four including a 16-year-old and wounding a woman. Gang violence keeps Esmeraldas and the other coastal provinces among Ecuador's deadliest.

title: Pakistani intelligence-based operation in Panjgur, Balochistan
summary: Pakistani security forces killed five militants in an intelligence-based operation in Panjgur district of Balochistan, according to the military's ISPR media wing. Weapons, ammunition and improvised explosive devices were recovered and destroyed at the site, with clearance operations continuing afterwards. The military labelled the group 'Fitna al-Hindustan', its official designation for Baloch separatists it alleges are backed by India.

title: Twin IEDs hit Somali army and Gorgor convoy near Awdheegle
summary: Al-Shabaab detonated two improvised explosive devices against Somali National Army convoys that included Gorgor special forces units near the town of Awdheegle in Lower Shabelle, on a key road roughly 45 miles southwest of Mogadishu. At least 10 soldiers were killed and at least 20 wounded, while al-Shabaab claimed the attacks caused 52 casualties. Other reporting on the same incident describes a single device on the Awdheegle-Mubarak road with higher tolls attributed to al-Shabaab (20+) and to a Somali journalist (30, including a commander); these are unverified. The strike underscored the group's continued ability to interdict elite units on main supply routes close to Mogadishu.

title: KIA intercepts junta column advancing on Mabein, northern Shan State
summary: Battalion 34 of the KIA's Brigade 4 intercepted a junta column of roughly 150 troops from Light Infantry Battalion 348 on 10-11 August near Upper and Lower Nyaungni villages (about 2 miles north of Momeik), blocking its advance toward KIA-held Mabein Township. The regime called in Mi-35 attack helicopters and a Y-12 aircraft, striking Mabein communities already inundated by flooding from upstream Shweli River dam releases. At least one regime soldier was confirmed killed; DVB reported no casualties from the Nyaungni airstrikes, only displacement. SSPP/SSA participation is flagged as unconfirmed in the source. Separate Mabein airstrike casualties reported by SHRF (4 killed, 8 injured) belong to a different window (28 July-8 August) and are not attributable to this clash.

title: Junta airstrike kills 14 in Kyauk Gyi village, Thandwe Township
actors: Arakan Army (AA, area control / reporting party)
summary: A junta air raid struck Kyauk Gyi village about 20 miles south of Thandwe town at around 1pm on 10 August, killing 14 people aged 9 to 88 — eleven of them female — and wounding 11 others while damaging 21 houses. Three high-explosive bombs fell near the Dhamma Yaung Chi monastery after a jet circled for roughly 20 minutes. The Arakan Army, which controls the area, said airstrikes hit around Thandwe almost daily. A separate strike on the Ngapali beach resort, injuring two and damaging some 20 resort buildings, occurred earlier on 3 August, not later that week. Toll converged upward across reports (10 → 12 → 14) and the 14 figure originates from an AA casualty list.

title: Troops repel ISWAP assault on Gajiram forward operating base, Borno
summary: ISWAP fighters launched a coordinated assault on the Forward Operating Base at Gajiram in Nganzai LGA at around 12:20 a.m. on Monday 10 August, temporarily breaching part of the perimeter defences. Troops of Operation Hadin Kai repelled the attack with sustained firepower; several soldiers were wounded and surveillance showed the attackers evacuating numerous dead and wounded fighters. No confirmed soldier deaths; the 'terrorists neutralised' figure is an unquantified military claim.

title: Al-Shabaab pushes into Matabaan district after Teedaan capture
summary: A village head in Matabaan district reported that al-Shabaab had advanced into the district following its capture of Teedaan on 2 August, a road junction town 55 miles east of Beledweyne. Matabaan is a district capital some 45 miles northeast of the Hiiraan regional capital, and the advance placed al-Shabaab closer to Hiiraan's main population centres, eroding federal gains held since the 2022 central Somalia counteroffensive. No fighting or casualties were reported in Matabaan itself on 11 August — this is an incremental territorial advance, not a battle, and the report rests on a single village head relayed by one analytical source. The district capital was not reported captured.

title: US Navy helicopter fires on Panama-flagged vessel running the Iran blockade in the Gulf of Oman
region: Gulf of Oman (international waters off Pakistan)
summary: A US Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles into the Panama-flagged container ship Vela Nova after its crew ignored warnings from personnel enforcing the American naval blockade of Iranian ports, disabling its steering. The strike occurred at about 07:58 UTC in international waters roughly 71 nautical miles off the coast of Pakistan in the eastern Gulf of Oman. All 17 crew were accounted for with no casualties; Israeli and US reporting described the aim point as the rudder while CENTCOM's account cited the engine room, with the master reporting damage to the stern and steering compartment. Two days later Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States could sustain the blockade of Iranian ports indefinitely by rotating ships. Exact coordinates were never published; the position is derived from the reported distance off the Jiwani-Gwadar coastline and is accurate to roughly plus or minus 40km.

title: Double-tap Houthi missile strike on cargo ship Tihamah in Bab el-Mandeb kills six
summary: Houthi forces fired ballistic missiles at the Egyptian-owned, Tanzania-flagged deck cargo ship Tihamah while it lay at anchor northeast of Perim Island after departing al-Makha. Three missiles struck the vessel, setting a fire that killed three Pakistani and one Indonesian crew member. A fourth missile was fired while a search-and-rescue operation was under way, killing two Yemeni National Resistance Forces personnel and bringing the toll to six. It was the first fatal Houthi attack on commercial shipping since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February 2026, and drew a statement from the IMO Secretary-General.

title: AFC/M23 bombardment of Chambombo and Lumbishi kills five civilians
summary: Shelling attributed to AFC/M23 hit inhabited areas and FARDC positions in the Kalehe localities of Chambombo and Lumbishi on 12 August, killing five civilians and wounding four Congolese soldiers, according to Major Dieudonné Kaseraka of the 34th Military Region. A precarious calm returned the following day but residents said the situation remained unpredictable.

title: North Korea launches ballistic missile 700km ahead of Ulchi Freedom Shield drills
actors: South Korea Joint Chiefs of Staff
summary: North Korea fired a ballistic missile from the Wonsan area at around 6 a.m. that flew more than 700 kilometres toward the Sea of Japan. It was Pyongyang's second ballistic launch in under a week and its 11th suspected ballistic missile test of 2026. The launch came as Seoul and Washington announced their annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise would begin on August 17.

title: Japan scrambles fighter jets as Chinese Y-9 reconnaissance aircraft transits East China Sea
summary: A Chinese Y-9 intelligence-gathering aircraft flew from mainland China across the East China Sea, passing south of Nagasaki Prefecture's Danjo Islands before turning southwest and reversing course northwest of Okinawa's main island back toward the mainland. Japan's Air Self-Defense Force Western Air Defense Force scrambled fighter jets in response. The Joint Staff release recorded no airspace violation; the aircraft remained over international waters. Japan logged 181 scrambles in April-June 2026, 139 of them against Chinese aircraft.
source_name: Japan Ministry of Defense Joint Staff

title: Iranian missile and drone barrage hits Kurdish opposition camps in Erbil province
summary: Over 11-12 August Iran fired five missiles and four drones at Iranian Kurdish opposition targets across the Alana, Balisan, Harir, Khalifan and Soran areas of Erbil province, roughly 60km northeast of the regional capital. Three missiles hit Komala's camp in the Alana valley on 11 August, wounding two; two more struck KDPI positions in Balisan on 12 August, while four one-way attack drones came down in Harir, Khalifan and central Soran, one damaging a civilian house, with no casualties. Rudaw reported on 14 August that the Kurdistan Region had recorded more than 950 drone and missile attacks since the outbreak of the six-week war in late February 2026, killing 32 and wounding 154 as of early August.
source_name: EPIC Iraq Security and Humanitarian Monitor

title: Arakan Army repels junta offensive across Yekyi and Thabaung townships
summary: Fighting erupted at five separate sites across Yekyi and Thabaung townships as the 1st, 11th and 101st Light Infantry Battalions of the junta's 66th Light Infantry Division pushed into northern Ayeyarwady Region. Engagements ran up to seven hours at the longest site (Point 101 Hill, Yekyi Township, 07:00-14:00), with three to four hours at Thar Paung Kalay and the Point 101 southwest approach, backed by fighter jets, Y-12 aircraft, attack drones and heavy artillery. The regime columns retreated, leaving behind military hardware, ammunition and the bodies of fallen soldiers that the AA recovered. No source gives a casualty number; all reporting traces to the AA's 13 August statement relayed by Rakhine outlets. Coordinates anchor on Thabaung town; three of the five sites lie in Yekyi Township some 60km away.

title: Fifteen of 18 PLA aircraft sorties cross Taiwan Strait median line in single day
summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 18 PLA aircraft sorties, 11 PLA Navy ships and three official vessels around Taiwan in its routine 6 a.m. to 6 a.m. daily tally, with 15 of the 18 sorties crossing the Taiwan Strait median line into Taiwan's air defence identification zone. Taiwan responded with combat air patrol aircraft, navy vessels and coastal missile systems. The MND did not characterise the activity as a joint combat readiness patrol, unlike the named operations reported on August 15 and August 18; the day was an elevated tally within the normal band rather than a discrete escalation.
source_name: GlobalSecurity.org / ROC Ministry of National Defense

title: Chinese survey ship under coast guard and militia escort maps Taiwan's EEZ east of Hualien
summary: The PRC research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 03, escorted by a China Coast Guard cutter and a maritime militia fishing vessel, ran repeated east-west survey patterns inside Taiwan's exclusive economic zone from August 13, ranging from the edge of Taiwan's contiguous zone near Hualien County to about 155 nautical miles east of the island. The survey was still running at the August 24 reporting cutoff, at least 12 days. The waters surveyed sit astride approach routes a PLA force would use to encircle Taiwan from the east. Unlike two earlier surveys, Beijing did not announce this mission, which AEI assesses as an attempt to normalise such activity without publicity; the CCG has maintained permanent patrols in Taiwan's EEZ out to 200 nautical miles east of the island since June 2026.

title: Fighting on the Igali axis at Kusisa kills four including a mother and two children
summary: Three days of intensifying combat on the Igali axis around Kusisa, in the Ziralo grouping of Kalehe territory, left at least four dead including a mother and her two children, with four FARDC soldiers wounded. The army claimed to have retaken Chambombo, Shanje, Lumbishi, Kavumu-Luzirantaka and Numbi, while civilians fled toward Masisi in North Kivu.

title: Four Chinese coast guard ships intrude into Japanese territorial waters off Senkaku Islands
summary: Four China Coast Guard vessels, Haijing 1301, 1302, 1304 and 1305, all machine-gun equipped, entered Japanese territorial waters around the Senkaku Islands at about 4 p.m. and departed roughly two hours later, after operating in the adjacent contiguous zone for a sixth consecutive day. The Japan Coast Guard shadowed the vessels and issued departure demands. It was the only territorial-waters intrusion recorded in August 2026, against contiguous-zone entries on 26 of 27 days. The incident followed the August 4 release of Japan's 2026 defence white paper, which describes China as an unprecedented and the greatest strategic challenge Japan faces.
source_name: Japan Coast Guard (11th Regional Coast Guard Headquarters)

title: Coalition forces intercept three bomb-laden drones over Erbil
actors: Kurdistan Directorate General of Counter Terrorism
summary: Between 2:17 am and 2:25 am, air defences of the US-led Global Coalition shot down three explosive-laden drones over Erbil city, according to the Kurdistan Region's Directorate General of Counter Terrorism. Footage showed wreckage from one drone falling near a residential project without causing damage or casualties. The attempted strike came two days after Iran's missile and drone barrage on Iranian Kurdish opposition camps northeast of the city.

title: Islamic State Sahel Province frees kidnapped US missionary
summary: American missionary pilot Kevin Rideout, a SIM International pilot abducted by three armed men from his Niamey home roughly 100 yards from the presidential palace on 21 October 2025, was released on 14 August 2026 after nearly 10 months in captivity. He was moved to northern Mali and held by Islamic State Sahel Province, which he confirmed after his release. Officials of Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army played a key role in securing his freedom; Reuters sources gave conflicting accounts of a brokered deal, a ransom payment, or a military rescue operation, so it remains unclear whether a ransom was paid.

title: Six ballistic missiles hit al-Makha port and moored vessels
summary: The Yemeni government said Houthi forces fired six ballistic missiles into al-Makha on Friday, striking port infrastructure and civilian assets and setting several fishing boats on fire. The government reported at least four civilians killed while a military official told AFP the toll was at least eight including two security personnel; the Houthis claimed they had destroyed boats and weapons belonging to Saudi-backed forces.

title: BLA claims 22-attack campaign across Balochistan over eight days
region: Balochistan (Chagai, Kharan, Kech, Kalat, Panjgur, Nushki, Turbat, Surab, Quetta)
summary: The Baloch Liberation Army claimed 22 separate attacks across Balochistan between 9 and 15 August 2026, saying 26 Pakistani military and government-backed personnel were killed. The claim was issued by BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch and first carried by The Balochistan Post, then amplified by Indian outlets (ANI, Republic World). Operations were claimed in Chagai, Kharan, Kech, Kalat, Panjgur, Nushki, Turbat, Surab and Quetta and included bombings of police posts, IED strikes on convoys, grenade attacks, vehicle seizures and destruction of surveillance equipment. The single largest sub-claim - 17 personnel killed in an IED attack on a military convoy at Rodenjo, Kalat - has no independent or official confirmation, and the BLA claimed the same figure for a separate July 2026 convoy attack near Bela. Pakistani authorities issued no comprehensive response. Independent ANI reporting of 10 August does confirm real attacks in the window (a Kech convoy strike, a Surab bridge demolition), but the aggregate toll is unverified and likely inflated.

title: KNLA overruns Kwimaungtaing village, triggering junta counteroffensive in Kawkareik
summary: KNLA-led forces overran junta positions at Kwimaungtaing village in Htihpoezan village tract, northern Kawkareik Township, forcing regime troops to abandon weapons and ammunition in the strategic foothills of the Dawna Range. The junta responded with air and ground strikes within 24 hours, advancing from Kyondoe and Nabu toward the Bote Road section, and on 22 August dispatched a nine-truck convoy carrying roughly 200 newly drafted conscripts from Hpa-An, with further reinforcements moving along Asian Highway 1. Single-newsroom sourcing: the only other carrier (BNI) republishes Karen Information Center, i.e. Karen News itself. No casualty figures published. Coordinates are the Kawkareik town centroid; the fighting is in northern Kawkareik Township, likely 15-25km further north.

title: Houthi missiles and drones hit Marib residential areas
summary: Marib's government media office said six ballistic missiles and four drones targeted residential neighbourhoods in the city on Saturday evening, wounding four people and damaging homes, vehicles and civilian infrastructure. Same-day reporting counted four missiles and four drones in the initial wave, with a fifth missile later in the day and a sixth overnight. Marib hosts more than two million internally displaced people, over 40 percent of Yemen's displaced population.

title: South Korea fires warning shots after North Korean troops cross Military Demarcation Line
summary: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff disclosed on August 16 that multiple North Korean soldiers had crossed the Military Demarcation Line in the inland eastern sector of the DMZ at an undisclosed point the previous week, prompting warning broadcasts and then warning shots under standing operational procedures. The North Korean troops withdrew to their side without returning fire and no casualties were reported. It was the South Korean military's first use of warning shots in 2026 and the first reported MDL violation of the year, against 17 recorded violations in 2025.

title: AA ambush destroys junta relief column bound for Nat Yay Kan radar base
summary: The Arakan Army ambushed a junta reinforcement column of roughly 200 troops moving toward the Nat Yay Kan air defence and radar installation, intercepting it as it advanced from Gotegyi (Gok Gyi) village under air cover and forcing it to retreat back into Gotegyi with heavy losses. BNI's dedicated report (DMG) puts the ambush on 16 August with nearly 50 regime personnel killed; a later summarising article dates it 15 August with approximately 60 killed including senior officers. Wounded were evacuated on 17 August to Artillery Battalion 905 at Padan. Nat Yay Kan is not in Ann Township, Rakhine State as first coded — it sits on the Ann-Padan road in Ngape Township, Minbu District, Magway Region, on the Rakhine-Magway boundary. Coordinates are the Ngape Township centroid; the site lies somewhat southwest, in the western Ngape hills.

title: Armed herders raid six villages in Ukum LGA, Benue State
summary: Gunmen on motorcycles laid siege to at least six communities in the Mbaterem council ward of Ukum LGA at around 4:30 a.m., firing sporadically and forcing residents to flee into the bush. Many were feared killed and several sustained gunshot wounds; Governor Hyacinth Alia blamed armed herders for the assault. Toll is contested: Benue Police confirmed 3 killed and 4 machete injuries at Aboajo village, while the constituency lawmaker and community sources plus Vanguard and Ripples report over 10 killed.

title: Renewed Houthi strikes on al-Makha outskirts kill four
summary: An overnight Houthi missile and drone attack struck the outskirts of al-Makha and a main road in the city, killing four people and injuring eight according to state media and the director of al-Makha airport, with port operations already suspended after several days of strikes. The Yemeni military said it launched 181 operations against Houthi positions in several governorates on Saturday and Sunday, killing and wounding dozens.

title: Indonesian military drone strikes pound TPNPB headquarters in Puncak Jaya
summary: The Indonesian military launched dozens of drone strikes from a base on a neighbouring mountain against the TPNPB headquarters compound in Puncak Jaya regency between 16 and 19 August, with waves of around ten drones on the opening day. The rebel group said the bombardment damaged the compound's grounds, walls and roofs through blast waves and fragments but reported no casualties.

title: Explosion at school in Dasht-e-Barchi, Kabul
summary: A grenade blast struck the private 'Shama-e Hidayat' school in the Mahdia neighbourhood (police district 18) of Kabul's Dasht-e-Barchi at around 4:30pm local time on 17 August 2026, as students were leaving classrooms. UNICEF and UNAMA reported at least 42 injured children aged 9-14; local outlets put the figure at 52 or more, and Kabul's Emergency Hospital alone received 35 injured children. No deaths were reported. Taliban police spokesman Khalid Zadran confirmed a hand grenade caused the blast and said an investigation was under way, and the Directorate of Mine Action Coordination confirmed a grenade detonated at the site. Causation remains contested: UNAMA cited 'conflicting reports of either an attack or unexploded ordnance', local sources described a grenade thrown from an alley opposite the school, while witnesses said the grenade exploded while in the possession of a student who was himself wounded. No group claimed responsibility. ISIS-K has repeatedly targeted the predominantly Hazara neighbourhood's schools and mosques.

title: AFC/M23 and Wazalendo battle in Ufamandu I, southern Masisi
summary: Heavy artillery exchanges between AFC/M23 and a Wazalendo coalition swept the Ufamandu I grouping of southern Masisi on 17 August, concentrated around Remeka and Kashovu. Several hundred families fled to safer locations including Remeka centre, Katuundu and Biriko as the Kalehe/Ziralo front spilled north across the South Kivu-North Kivu boundary, emptying villages along the axis.

title: Somali federal troops drive Laftagareen loyalists out of Baidoa
summary: Fighters loyal to ousted South West state president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen — who resigned on 30 March 2026 hours after federal troops and allied opposition militias seized Baidoa, then fled abroad — attacked federal troops in Baidoa at dawn using vehicle-borne explosives, triggering the fiercest urban combat in the city since March. Federal soldiers pushed the militiamen out of the centre, with the defence ministry claiming around 30 opposition fighters killed; a local elder counted 10 bodies including four civilians and six soldiers from both sides. The defence ministry publicly framed the attackers as al-Shabaab-aligned, a label Laftagareen's camp rejects; the better-supported reading is a widening federal-state rupture over constitutional powers and electoral autonomy rather than the al-Shabaab war.

title: Iranian drones strike Kurdistan Region PM Masrour Barzani's private office in Pirmam
summary: Two explosive-laden Hadid-110 one-way attack drones launched from Iranian territory targeted the private office of Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani and the residence of the head of the Parastin security agency in Erbil's Pirmam district at about 12:28 am. The Counter-Terrorism Directorate statement did not clarify whether the drones hit their targets; no casualties were reported. The KRG called it a dangerous escalation and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein demanded an official clarification from Tehran in a call with his Iranian counterpart. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied responsibility, said he had no information the drones were launched from Iranian territory, and suggested the attack was staged to drive a wedge between Tehran and the Kurds. The US, UK, EU and Saudi Arabia condemned the attack.

title: Iraqi counter-terrorism forces arrest and then release Nujaba intelligence chief
summary: Iraq's Counter-Terrorism Service detained Abbas Hussein al-Yaqoubi, a senior Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba figure and PMF intelligence officer, in the al-Fadhliya subdistrict of Suq al-Shuyukh district, Dhi Qar, on charges tied to attacks on US interests. He was handed to PMF security custody within about a day and formally released on 19 August after a judge dismissed the charges, a reversal analysts attributed to fears of armed escalation with Nujaba, which had compared the arrest to the Saddam era and whose supporters threatened to storm the Green Zone. The episode became a test case for the Iraqi government's stalled campaign to bring Iran-aligned factions under state control.
source_name: EPIC Iraq Security and Humanitarian Monitor

title: Iraqi F-16s destroy ISIS position in Wadi Zghaytoun, Kirkuk
summary: Iraq's Security Media Cell reported that Iraqi Air Force F-16s bombed a position used by suspected Islamic State militants in the Wadi Zghaytoun area of Kirkuk province, in the Hamrin belt south of Kirkuk city. The strike destroyed the position and killed an unspecified number of militants. It formed part of a wider counter-ISIS effort in the northern disputed territories that month.
source_name: EPIC Iraq Security and Humanitarian Monitor

title: Iran seizes UAE-linked tanker in the Strait of Hormuz
summary: Iranian state media reported that the IRGC had detained the Liberia-flagged products tanker Amara (IMO 9333280), described as UAE-linked, for violating Tehran's new rules for transiting the Strait of Hormuz, which require vessels to follow an Iranian-designated route and pay transit fees. AIS tracking showed a sharp course deviation southeast of Qeshm Island, toward which the vessel was escorted, and it remained in Iranian waters as of 19 August. Reuters noted the detaining authority was not independently identified and that neither Iranian nor UAE authorities officially confirmed the seizure. Iran went on to publish a blacklist of 45 tankers on 23 August for breaching the same rules.

title: Junta shelling of DKBA outpost strands 2,000 displaced civilians on Thai border
actors: Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA, junta-aligned proxy — target of the shelling)
summary: Junta artillery fired on the DKBA's No. 915 Kyun Taw base in the Hpalu-Minletpan area of southern Myawaddy Township at around 6pm on 17 August, striking an outpost adjacent to the Palaw Ta Po displacement camp near the Thaungyin (Moei) River. Two DKBA members were killed and nearly 20 of their family members wounded, including women and children, and evacuated to Kyauk Khat Hospital. More than 2,000 internally displaced people sheltering in the Hpalu-Minletpan area were left trapped, unable to cross into Thailand because of monsoon river levels. Confirmed independently by Karen News/KIC, m-CDM via moemaka, and Burma Coup Resistance Notes; sources differ on one shell versus three. Note this was the junta shelling its own aligned proxy, not a junta-resistance engagement. Coordinates are interpolated toward the Moei River within southern Myawaddy Township — no gazetteer entry exists for Palaw Ta Po, Hpalu or Minletpan.

title: Azerbaijan issues warrants for Russian media figures, summons ambassador
summary: Azerbaijani prosecutors charged three Russian media figures - transportation ministry adviser Alexei Chadayev, commentator Semyon Uralov and Moscow 24 presenter Ivan Knyazev - with calls for the violent overthrow of the Azerbaijani government and incitement over July-August livestreams, and Baku summoned Russia's ambassador the next day. Chadayev resigned his government post; the episode extended the strain in Azerbaijan-Russia relations that has persisted since the December 2024 downing of an AZAL passenger plane.

title: KKB attack on Jila military post kills Indonesian soldier on Independence Day
region: Jila District, Mimika Regency, Central Papua
summary: Separatist fighters attacked the Posramil Jila military post in Mimika Regency as Indonesia marked its 81st Independence Day, triggering a firefight that killed Private Rizki Kurniawan and wounded two other soldiers. The assault was one of several coordinated KKB shootings across Highland and Central Papua around the 17 August anniversary.

title: Thai sergeant major loses leg to PMN-2 mine near Chong An Ma crossing
region: Nam Yuen District, Ubon Ratchathani (Thai-Cambodian border)
summary: Sergeant Major Channarong Wongchana of the 2nd Battalion, 2nd Infantry Regiment stepped on a PMN-2 anti-personnel mine during a clearance operation at Chong An Ma in Ubon Ratchathani, severing his lower right leg and badly wounding his right hand. It was the fifteenth amputation suffered by a Thai soldier since border hostilities with Cambodia erupted in 2025, in an area Thai forces had retaken from Cambodian troops.

title: M23 counteroffensive seizes the entire Ziralo grouping in Kalehe
summary: After a DRC coalition attack on 17 August, M23 launched a counteroffensive and captured Kashobo, Katenderi, Kivocat, Matutira, Mutale and Tushunguti on 18 August, then Mianda, Charamba and Lulere the next day. By 19 August the whole Ziralo grouping had reverted to M23 control, reversing the FARDC-Wazalendo gains of the preceding week and displacing more than 815 households toward Ramba.
source_name: Critical Threats (AEI), Congo War Security Review, August 21, 2026

title: Drone strike hits farmer training centre at Dandera near Mekelle
summary: A drone struck a farmer training centre at Dandera village, roughly 15km east-southeast of the Tigrayan capital Mekelle, at around 10:00 local time, hitting farmland near a school and a livestock watering hole. Tigrayan authorities blamed the federal government in Addis Ababa and said no one was hurt, but a local priest told AFP he saw one fighter killed and believed two others were wounded, and the BBC independently reported one killed and one wounded. It was the first strike of a series that brought the air campaign to the outskirts of Mekelle.

title: Junta jets bomb gold mining sites at Maing Tone Tar Gyi, Pinlebu Township
summary: Myanmar Air Force jets bombed gold mining sites near Maing Tone Tar Gyi village, some 22 miles (35km) northeast of Pinlebu town, at approximately 11am. DVB reported at least four civilians killed and four missing; AAPP and moemaka's CDM digest both report six killed (four women, two men). The area has been under National Unity Government administration since resistance forces seized Pinlebu in October 2024 after a 53-day battle, and the strike capped a series of raids from 16 August that also hit Kinpan Hospital (16 Aug) and Mansi Hospital (17 Aug); residents attribute the accuracy of the targeting to intelligence leaks from a BNRA defector, a claim sourced only to DVB. Coordinates are derived from the source's own bearing and distance from Pinlebu town (24.0814N, 95.3703E); no gazetteer entry exists for the village, so precision is roughly ±8km.

title: Machete massacre kills at least 25 in Bin-Per village, Plateau State
summary: Armed men stormed the village of Bin-Per in Kombun District, Mangu LGA, late on Monday 17 August and moved house to house killing residents with machetes into the early hours of 18 August, leaving 20-26 dead, mostly women and children (Vanguard and Bernama 24, Guardian 26, AP and Amnesty 'at least 25'). The massacre followed the killing of two herders the previous week and a suspected reprisal attack that torched homes in nearby Maitimbe.

title: Yemeni army reports 133 operations against Houthis in 24 hours across multiple fronts
summary: Army spokesperson Colonel Majed al-Nuzaili said government forces conducted at least 133 operations against Houthi capabilities and personnel in a single 24-hour period, part of a broad escalation following the August 6 missile salvo. Fighting was active simultaneously across Marib, al-Jawf, Hadramawt, Taiz, Hodeidah, al-Dhale and Lahj, marking the widest multi-front combat since the 2022 truce. The figure is a government operational claim relayed from a single armed forces statement and carries no released casualty count or independent battle-damage confirmation. Coordinates anchor on Marib, the principal front, as the event has national scope rather than a single location.

title: KKB abducts nine women and girls, kills mother in Pasir Putih village, Mimika
region: Jila District, Mimika Regency, Central Papua
summary: Armed separatists stormed Pasir Putih village in Jila District, Mimika, taking nine women and girls hostage into the forest, including a pregnant 17-year-old and three elementary school pupils. A mother was shot dead for resisting capture and her child was thrown into a ravine, breaking a leg; security forces deployed a Brimob unit by helicopter and senior commanders took charge of the pursuit and rescue operation.

title: TB2 drone strike on Mwalu Hotel in Fizi-centre
summary: Two bombs dropped by TB2-type drones struck the Mwalu Hotel in Fizi-centre at around 1 a.m. on 19 August, tearing off the roof and seriously injuring two civilians including the hotel manager; no deaths were reported. The FARDC's Sukola 2 sector blamed AFC/M23-Twirwaneho with drones piloted from Rwanda. Local sources said the hotel had hosted senior Congolese and Burundian FDNB officers planning a new push toward Minembwe; the officers had left before the strike, and arrests followed amid suspicion of an intelligence leak. Twirwaneho denied responsibility and accused the FARDC of staging the attack.

title: Iranian missiles fired toward the UAE trigger a total Emirati trade embargo on Iran
summary: The UAE said Iran launched two missiles toward its territory on the night of 18 August, one falling outside and one inside Emirati territorial waters, causing no casualties or damage, and announced early on 19 August that all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran were halted until further notice. Iran denied firing the missiles and called the incident a baseless false flag. The embargo threatened to close Iran's most important remaining economic escape route, the UAE having supplied over 30 percent of Iranian imports. Analysts at Kpler told CNN the previous day that Iran had at least partially lost control of the Strait of Hormuz as traffic shifted to a UN-authorised Omani transit corridor. No source published the missile splashdown position; coordinates are an approximation in UAE waters north of Abu Dhabi.

title: Arakan Army storms three junta outposts on the Ann-Padan highway
summary: On the evening of 19 August the AA launched a coordinated overnight assault on three temporary junta camps — two near Gok Gyi (Gotegyi) village and one between Pazhi village and Nat Yay Kan Mountain — along the Ann-Padan highway on the Rakhine-Magway boundary. The attack combined weaponised drones, sniper fire, artillery and close-quarters infantry assault; the camps were damaged and regime casualties were evacuated toward Padan. Corrected geography: the action is in Ngape Township, Minbu District, Magway Region, anchored on Gôkkyi (19.8586N, 94.4419E), not Ann Township in Rakhine State some 30km west. Padan is a village in Ngape Township hosting Artillery Battalion HQ 905, not a township. Severity held at 3 on strategic significance (year-long siege of the Nat Yay Kan air-defence node) rather than casualties, which the source leaves unquantified. Primary source is Narinjara, 19 Aug; BNI republishes it.

title: North Korea fires more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles as US-South Korea drills end
actors: South Korea Joint Chiefs of Staff
summary: North Korea launched more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area at about 5 p.m., flying roughly 300 kilometres into waters east of the peninsula. Seoul's defence ministry assessed the weapons as likely 600mm multiple rocket launchers of the KN-25 type, which Pyongyang claims can carry tactical nuclear warheads. The salvo came on the penultimate day of the scaled-back Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise, which ran August 17-21, and Seoul convened an emergency national security meeting and condemned the launches as a violation of UN Security Council resolutions.

title: Drone strikes on Mekelle residential areas wound 13 including five children
summary: Two drone strikes hit the Tigrayan capital Mekelle early in the morning, the first in Hawelti sub-city (Momona Kebele) near St Mary Church where residential homes were damaged and a second reported near Mekelle University — a location attributed to the TPLF leader, with Addis Standard instead placing it in the Kuha area. Ayder Specialized Hospital received 13 casualties aged 2 to 60, including five children and seven women, three of them seriously hurt; no deaths were reported by any source. Tigrayan authorities blamed the federal government; the national army did not immediately comment, and analysts read the strikes as Addis Ababa signalling willingness to use harsher means against the TPLF.

title: Resistance ambushes rout junta column on the Pathein-Monywa road in Mindon
actors: USBA (rendered 'United States of Burma Army' by the source; expansion unstable)
Local resistance / PDF (Thayet District PDF Battalion No. 4)
summary: A junta column of roughly 100 troops that left Mindon on 20 August along the Pathein-Monywa road, aiming to reach Shante Police Station in Minhla, was hit by a series of coordinated ambushes between 20 and 26 August, losing more than 20 soldiers killed and nearly 30 wounded before collapsing and retreating under artillery cover to the Kyauktaing outpost in Mindon Township. Resistance forces claim they seized a military truck, a power generator and ammunition; a Buddhist nun was injured by regime shelling in Mindon Township's Uyinpu village. Reinforcement attempts from 24 August were also ambushed. Note the BNI headline slug says 'Minhla' but every combat location in the article body is in Mindon Township — the record's title is correct and the source headline is the error. USBA is a real, independently attested actor in this corridor, but 'United States of Burma Army' is almost certainly a machine-translation artifact; store the acronym as canonical. Casualty figures rest on a single USBA claim relayed by one outlet with no independent or regime confirmation; a separate MPA Press report gives 15 killed on 23 August between Kyoetwa and Ywa Thit. Coordinates are Mindon town, the column's stated departure point.
source_name: Burma News International / Network Media Group

title: Pakistan says 49 militants killed in high-tempo KP and Balochistan raids
region: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Bannu, North Waziristan, Orakzai, Khyber) and Balochistan (Mastung, Mach, Khuzdar, Panjgur)
summary: Pakistan's military said security forces working with police killed 49 militants in a series of intelligence-driven joint raids conducted over several days, with 12 killed in Bannu, North Waziristan, Orakzai and Khyber districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and 37 killed in 10 intelligence-based operations across Mastung, Mach, Khuzdar and Panjgur in Balochistan. ISPR labelled the KP militants 'Fitna al-Khawarij' (TTP) and the Balochistan militants 'Fitna al-Hindustan' (Baloch separatists). Explosives, weapons, ammunition, IED detonating remotes and motorcycles were seized and destroyed. No security force or civilian casualties were reported. The raids marked a widening of operations amid a sharp surge in militant violence.

title: Junta airstrike on Buddhist monastery kills 14 in Myaung Township
summary: A military fighter jet, reportedly flying from Tada-U airbase, bombed a Buddhist monastery in Swel Le Oh village, Myaung Township, about 75km west of Mandalay, where more than 100 people had gathered for a weeklong retreat during Buddhist Lent. At least 14 people were killed, including three women and the abbot, and 20 were wounded; later tallies reached 15 killed and 28 wounded. AP reports two bombs 15 minutes apart, the local outlet LuduNwayOo reports four. Multiply and independently sourced (Al Jazeera, AP, AFP, plus same-day Burmese local reporting from LuduNwayOo/People's Spring and Global Arakan Network); confirmed distinct from the 11 July 2025 Lin Ta Lu monastery strike in Sagaing Township. Coordinates anchor on Myaung town, which fits the reported 75km from Mandalay better than the original point; Swel Le Oh has no gazetteer entry. The claim that Myaung was flood-affected could not be confirmed.

title: BLA IED and ambush on military convoy at Khadkocha, Mastung
summary: An IED planted in the Gro (Goru) area of Khadkocha, Mastung district, along the Quetta-Karachi National Highway (N-25), was detonated against passing security force vehicles on the night of 22 August 2026, followed by a heavy exchange of fire. Pakistani outlets reported 1-2 security personnel killed and 6-8 wounded, with casualties taken to Nawab Ghaus Bakhsh Raisani Memorial Hospital in Mastung; the highway was closed, helicopters were deployed and a search operation launched. The Baloch Liberation Army, via spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch, claimed responsibility and asserted a far higher toll of 13 military personnel killed and more than 10 wounded, with two armoured vehicles destroyed - figures that are unverified and roughly six to ten times the independently reported toll. The Balochistan Home Department imposed an indefinite curfew in Khadkocha and adjoining areas from 7:00am on 23 August 2026.

title: DRC and AFC/M23 agree Doha framework roadmap after talks near Montreux
summary: After five days of closed-door talks near Montreux, Switzerland from 17 to 21 August, Kinshasa and the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 issued a joint statement on 22 August announcing a roadmap setting sequenced steps and timelines for negotiations under the Doha Framework Agreement signed on 15 November 2025. The parties also agreed a standardised method for reporting alleged ceasefire violations and a mechanism to review implementation of existing commitments. Talks were facilitated by Qatar, the United States, Togo as AU mediator, the AU Commission and Switzerland; analysts noted only one of seven Doha protocols has been settled.

title: BRP Diego Silang faces down five Chinese ships at Escoda Shoal
summary: The Philippine frigate BRP Diego Silang (FFG-7) conducted a maritime domain awareness exercise near Escoda (Sabina) Shoal while confronting five Chinese vessels, a mix of PLA Navy warships and China Coast Guard ships, that tailed it and tried to force a course change. The frigate issued repeated radio challenges asserting Philippine sovereign rights as a Chinese sailor claimed Beijing's 'indisputable sovereignty' over the low-tide feature inside the Philippine exclusive economic zone.

title: ADF kill 16 civilians and abduct children across Mambasa villages
summary: At least 16 civilians were killed in a week of ADF incursions across five villages of Mambasa territory, in the Babila-Babombi chiefdom along the Mambasa-Biakato axis, with the latest raids on Sunday 23 August hitting Ngombari, Kalonge and Seseo. Eight people were killed and eight children abducted into the bush in those attacks, prompting local civil society to demand reinforced military operations. Other outlets put the toll since 21 August as high as 24.

title: ISIS militants attack PMF 63rd Brigade outpost near Tuz Khormatu
summary: Islamic State fighters assaulted an outpost of the Popular Mobilization Forces' 63rd Brigade in the Tuz Khormatu district of Salah ad-Din province, in the Marssa Ali mountain area, before withdrawing after an exchange of fire; the attack was repulsed without casualties. It underlined a persistent ISIS presence in the Hamrin belt at a time when PMF units were heavily preoccupied by the confrontation with US and Saudi forces.
source_name: EPIC Iraq Security and Humanitarian Monitor

title: Junta supply flotilla fights upriver on the Ayeyarwady toward besieged Bhamo
summary: A junta riverine flotilla of 14-15 vessels including two armed escort craft left Mandalay's Gaw Wein jetty (KNG reports 19 August, Irrawaddy 21 August) carrying weapons, ammunition and provisions upriver to relieve besieged bases in Kachin State, docking at Katha on the evening of 25 August. Escorting airstrikes and artillery hit riverside villages: four civilians including a child were killed at Kyuntaw near Shwegu on 23-24 August, one more at Kalon village on the Katha-Tigyaing border, and a monastery chapel at Sithaw was destroyed; a conscripted civilian driver was killed near Palaungtaung on 23 August amid reports of commandeered vehicles and human shields. KIA and allied forces struck back with suicide drones near Thinbawin village east of Shwegu, setting two troop-carrying boats ablaze, and in a 24 August FPV strike near Zinbon, after which 100+ troops reportedly surrendered at Thabeik Inn. Anchored on Shwegu town (Kachin State, Bhamo District), the centroid of the reported violence, and dated to that violence rather than the Mandalay departure. Severity 4 rests on strategic significance, not the confirmed toll of roughly five civilians. Do not merge with the near-identical July-September 2025 flotilla operation. The '500km' figure appears in no source and has been dropped.

title: Gunmen kill two security operatives in Jol District, Riyom LGA
summary: Suspected armed attackers struck the Tanjol and Tarai communities of Jol District in Riyom LGA at about 2:30 p.m. on Sunday 23 August, triggering a firefight with responding security personnel. Two security operatives were killed and several injured, with the attackers seizing firearms from the dead; one civilian was reported missing.

title: Assault on Bodana border post near Ivorian frontier, Burkina Faso
summary: Heavy detonations and sustained gunfire were heard around 9 p.m. on Sunday 23 August 2026 at the Burkinabè border post of Bodana (Kampti department, Poni province), roughly 800 m from the Ivorian post of Kodiénou and about 15 km north of Doropo. Burkinabè authorities issued no confirmation and the precise nature of the incident remains unknown — reported hypotheses are an attack by an unidentified armed or terrorist group on the Bodana post, or a clash between Burkinabè forces and armed elements. Ivorian forces and gendarmerie reinforced surveillance and alert posture in the Kodiénou sector; no rounds struck Ivorian territory and no casualties or damage were reported on that side. No casualty toll was released by either side.

title: Viv Ansanm night assault on Kenscoff kills 47, over 50 kidnapped
summary: Gunmen of the Viv Ansanm coalition stormed Kenscoff's town center on the night of 23 August, attacking homes and a church sheltering people already displaced by gang violence. At least 47 people were killed and more than 50 kidnapped in what is believed to be Haiti's largest mass abduction in recent years, with a gang leader threatening to execute hostages if security forces kill gang members. The government deployed reinforcements, pledging that Kenscoff would not be abandoned.

title: US strike destroys drug semi-submersible in Eastern Pacific
summary: The US military struck a semi-submersible vessel in the Eastern Pacific on 23 August, killing two people it described as narco-terrorists. The strike ended a two-month pause in the US campaign against alleged drug boats in Latin American waters that has killed at least 227 people across 68 strikes since September 2025.

title: First DRC-M23 ceasefire verification mission deploys to Minembwe
summary: A joint verification team of Congolese government experts and AFC/M23 representatives, with African Union, Qatari and US observers, flew by MONUSCO helicopter to Minembwe in Fizi territory — the first field mission of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+/MCVE+) agreed in Doha on 14 October 2025. Kinshasa has accused M23 of killing more than 300 people in June and July while M23 alleges government artillery attacks near Minembwe. A second verification mission was announced but its site was left for AFC/M23 to choose.

title: Armed clashes between Harki tribesmen and security forces near Lanaz refinery, Khabat
summary: Armed clashes erupted overnight between members of the Harki tribe and security forces in the Khabat district west of Erbil, with gunfire heard near the Lanaz oil refinery, the site of a previous standoff between the tribe and security forces. Erbil police reported several arrests following the disturbances in Karda-Rasha village and gave no further details; no casualties were reported. The clashes highlighted friction over control of energy infrastructure inside the Kurdistan Region while it was simultaneously absorbing repeated Iranian drone and missile strikes.
source_name: EPIC Iraq Security and Humanitarian Monitor

title: Junta airstrike destroys school in Seinnyinwa village, Paletwa Township
actors: Arakan Army (AA, area control / reporting party)
summary: Two junta jets bombed a monastic primary school in Seinnyinwa (Sein Nyin Wa) village, Paletwa Township, in AA-controlled southern Chin State, while classes were in session, destroying the school building and 17 homes. DVB reports five killed including two children and 17 injured including nine children, six critically; the AA's 24 August statement gives the same figures. The strike formed part of a bombardment campaign running 2-24 August that killed six and wounded 28 in Paletwa township-wide, contributing to a combined Rakhine-Chin toll of 33 killed and 78 wounded — 111 casualties, which is what the source means by August civilian casualties passing 100 (no internal contradiction). Severity raised from 2 to 3: a mass-casualty strike on a functioning school. The 'hundreds of bombs over 20 minutes to an hour' descriptor characterises the wider August campaign, not this strike. Coordinates are Paletwa town (township seat); the village has no gazetteer entry.

title: Houthi ballistic missile sets fire to Saudi supertanker Amzan off Yanbu
summary: The Houthis struck the Saudi-flagged VLCC Amzan (IMO 9693745) roughly 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu in the early hours of Monday, calling the hit accurate and direct and saying a fire broke out aboard as nearby ships fled. UKMTO reported only an unknown projectile causing a main-deck fire; owner Bahri confirmed a security-related incident and said all crew were safe, without naming a weapon or attributing the attack. The Egyptian Navy responded to the distress call. The position lies in international waters near the Egypt-Saudi median line and is attributed to Saudi Arabia by flag, ownership and destination. Yanbu is Saudi Arabia's principal Red Sea oil export terminal and its main alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Armenia announces intention to apply for EU membership
summary: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told parliament that Armenia would begin preparing a formal application for EU membership in the near future, a historic geopolitical shift away from Russia's orbit, with a referendum on accession to follow only after the application is lodged. Moscow has pressed Yerevan to instead put EU-versus-Eurasian Economic Union membership to a referendum, keeping the move a live source of Russia-Armenia friction.

title: Bandits ambush Gusau-Funtua highway convoy in Tsafe LGA, Zamfara
summary: Gunmen blocked the Gusau-Funtua federal highway near Unguwar Chida village in Tsafe LGA at about 4:05 p.m. on Tuesday 25 August and attacked two commercial vehicles, killing eight travellers, abducting eight and wounding nine by gunfire. Police from Tsafe division and the Violence Crime Response Unit pursued the attackers and claimed to have killed 17 suspected bandits, a single-statement figure republished verbatim across outlets and not independently verified.

title: Government forces repel Houthi assault at al-Safa near Taiz
summary: Yemen's armed forces media centre said eight Houthi fighters were killed and 15 wounded when government troops thwarted a Tuesday attack in the al-Safa area on the Kalabah front, northeast of Taiz city; the statement was released on Wednesday 26 August. In separate fighting on Yemen's west coast some 150 km away, the government-aligned National Resistance Forces reported three of its soldiers killed after fierce clashes involving various types of weaponry. Casualty figures are one-sided government claims with no neutral or Houthi-side confirmation.

title: US strike on alleged drug boat in Caribbean kills four
summary: The US military launched a lethal strike on an alleged drug vessel travelling through established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean on 25 August, killing all four people aboard. It was the second strike in three days after a two-month lull, signalling the resumption of the US 'narco-terrorism' interdiction campaign in the region.

title: Operations Jericó and Factoría strike Los Choneros and Los Lobos networks
summary: Ecuadorian police launched simultaneous operations Jericó and Factoría in the early hours of 26 August, targeting the Los Choneros and Los Lobos criminal structures across Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos and a fourth province, with support from the US Southern Command and DEA. The raids produced 43 arrests including suspects already held inside prisons, seized around US$1 million in cash, roughly a tonne of cocaine and a light aircraft, and flagged 127 phantom companies allegedly used to launder gang proceeds.

title: Pakistani forces kill 11 militants in South Waziristan, Bannu and Khuzdar
region: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (South Waziristan, Bannu) and Balochistan (Khuzdar)
summary: Pakistan's ISPR said security forces killed 11 militants in intelligence-based operations, five in the Ladha area of South Waziristan, two in Bannu and four in the Sasool area of Khuzdar district of Balochistan. Weapons and ammunition were recovered and a militant hideout in Bannu was destroyed; the Khuzdar militants were targeted with quadcopter assistance. The military attributed the KP militants to the TTP ('Fitna al-Khawarij') and the Khuzdar militants to Baloch separatists ('Fitna al-Hindustan'). The raids came five days after a larger sweep announced on 22 August that the military said killed 49 militants across the same two provinces. The casualty count rests on a single official claim and was not independently verified on the ground.

title: RDF and UPDF hold eighth proximity commanders' meeting in Mbarara
summary: Commanders of units deployed along the Rwanda-Uganda border met in Mbarara, Uganda, for the eighth quarterly proximity commanders' meeting, led by Maj Gen Ruki Karusisi of the RDF 5 Infantry Division and Maj Gen Paul Muhanguzi of the UPDF 2 Infantry Division. The three-day session reviewed border security conditions and coordination mechanisms, with both sides urging open channels of communication and confidence-building; it was preceded by a joint tree-planting in Kamwezi Sub-County, Rukiga District. The previous meeting was held in Musanze, Rwanda, in February 2026. Note: the source contains no DRC or M23 content; relevance to this feed rests only on actor overlap (Karusisi was US-sanctioned in March 2026 over RDF support to M23).

title: Ambush on IT Road kills four Liangmai Naga civilians in Kangpokpi
summary: Suspected militants ambushed civilians travelling along the Imphal-Tamenglong (IT) Road between Makui and Thanamba in Manipur's Kangpokpi district, killing four members of the Liangmai Naga community, injuring one and leaving another missing. Police had not formally identified the assailants, though Indian media reports attributed the ambush to Kuki militants, stoking fresh Naga-Kuki tensions in a state already scarred by ethnic conflict since May 2023.

title: Mass rallies at Indonesian parliament on anniversary of deadly 2025 protests
summary: Students, workers and grassroots groups rallied at the national parliament in Jakarta against lavish lawmaker allowances and government spending priorities, one year after the August 2025 protest wave that left at least 10 dead and thousands arrested. Authorities deployed at least 18,000 police personnel around the parliamentary complex and boosted security in other cities, closing roads as further rallies were planned for 28 August.

title: FARC dissident commander 'Felipe' killed in Valle del Cauca military operation
actors: EMC Jaime Martínez front (Iván Mordisco faction)
summary: Colombian soldiers killed the dissident commander known as 'Felipe' or 'Arcadio', a key leader of the Jaime Martínez front of Iván Mordisco's EMC dissident faction, during a military operation in southwest Colombia on 30 August. President Abelardo de la Espriella called the killing a 'crushing blow', blaming Felipe for the April Cali-Buenaventura highway bombing that killed 20 people, as well as extortion and other attacks around Dagua.

title: Rival Libyan factions sign UN-backed roadmap for elections within two years
summary: Representatives of Libya's rival eastern and western governments signed an agreement at UNSMIL headquarters in Tripoli committing to legislative and presidential elections under a single executive authority within 24 months, after the UN-backed 4+4 committee initialled the draft in Tunis on 20 August. The deal provides for restructuring the election commission and reviewing disputed electoral laws, though analysts caution the core dispute over who governs in the interim remains unresolved.

title: Militants attack Kuki village in Kangpokpi, three villagers killed
summary: Suspected militants attacked the Kuki village of N. Teikhang in Manipur's Kangpokpi district, killing three villagers including two women and injuring four others. Coming four days after the IT Road ambush on Naga travellers in the same district, the attack deepened fears of a renewed cycle of inter-community violence in Manipur, where ethnic strife since May 2023 has killed around 260 people and displaced 60,000.
